scope.description: One probe on a three-voter cluster in which node 1 is a bare raft leader, node 2 a bare raft follower and node 3 is driven through the Node API. The probe first proposes through node 3's Node while it is still a member, then removes node 3 on the leader, lets node 3's application apply the committed entry, and repeats the same proposal with the same caller timeout.
assumptions: The harness plays the application loop for node 3 (handing Ready structs back with Advance) and the transport for all messages, delivering peer messages to node 3 through Node.Step so that raft state is only touched by the owning goroutine for the Node-driven node.
Node 1 is made leader directly by becomeCandidate/becomeLeader and then broadcasts its entry, which is the same leader state a completed election produces.
The subject's proposal is made through Node.Propose, the same call an embedding service uses, with a context that expires after the recorded timeout.
The derived field blocked_until_deadline is computed as (returned error == context.DeadlineExceeded) and (elapsed >= timeout/2); both operands are reported.
Delivery is fault-free and in-process; no restart, snapshot or leadership change occurs.
excluded: A non-expiring caller context, which the harness does not measure directly
ReadOnlyLeaseBased, snapshots, restarts and joint configurations
The embedding service's propagation and retry policy for proposals

basis.prefix: Harness (draft file assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, execution package '.'; no captured file is replaced). The test builds three storages for voters {1,2,3}: bare raft instances for nodes 1 and 2 and a RawNode wrapped in newNode for node 3, whose run loop is started and stopped by the test. A delivery pump sends each message to the instance it addresses, feeding node 3's messages through Node.Step so only the run loop touches that raft instance; a drive loop hands node 3's Readys back with storage.Append and Node.Advance, applies any committed conf-change entry through Node.ApplyConfChange, and moves the Ready's messages into the delivery queue. The probe makes node 1 leader (becomeCandidate, becomeLeader, bcastAppend), drives until both bare followers committed the leadership entry, and emits node_setup with probe_id 'member', leader, term, committed, node3_in_config and the call timeout. It then calls Node.Propose on node 3 with a 200 ms context and emits node_propose for probe_id 'member' with the error text, elapsed milliseconds, the timeout, the derived blocked_until_deadline and node3_in_config. Next it proposes a ConfChangeV2 removing node 3 on the bare leader, drives until node 3's configuration no longer contains node 3, and emits self_removal_applied with probe_id 'removed', node3_in_config, voters, node3_lead, node3_state and committed. Finally it repeats the same Node.Propose call with the same timeout and emits node_propose for probe_id 'removed'. The test asserts that the member control returns without error and that the post-removal call blocks until the deadline, so a change in either behaviour fails the harness instead of reshaping the evidence.
basis.responsibility: The Node API owns telling a caller whether a proposal can be admitted. When the library itself has learned that the node is no longer a member, a proposal call that cannot be processed must be reported as not admissible rather than blocking until the caller's context expires, leaving the caller to infer the reason from a deadline error.

comparisons.description: After the node applied its own removal, a proposal through the Node API is reported as not admissible instead of blocking until the caller's deadline.
Control: while the node is still a member, the same proposal call returns promptly without error.
